Cytomegalovirus retinitis causes progressive vision loss and can lead to blindness.
People with CD4 counts below 50 are at highest risk for CMV disease.

Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is a brain infection caused by the JC virus.
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome can cause worsening of opportunistic infections after starting ART.
TB screening at every HIV clinic visit should include asking about cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats.

TB-IRIS can present as worsening TB symptoms after ART is started.
Extrapulmonary TB is more common in people living with HIV.

Bedaquiline is a key medicine used in the treatment of drug-resistant TB in people with HIV.
Hepatitis B virus co-infection affects approximately 10 percent of people living with HIV globally.

Stopping tenofovir in people with hepatitis B co-infection can cause a hepatitis flare.
Liver function tests should be monitored regularly in people with HIV and hepatitis B.
Hepatitis C co-infection accelerates liver disease in people living with HIV.
Direct-acting antivirals can cure hepatitis C in people living with HIV.

Liver cirrhosis is a serious complication of untreated hepatitis co-infection in people with HIV.
Hepatocellular carcinoma risk is increased in people with HIV and hepatitis B or C co-infection.
All people living with HIV should be tested for hepatitis B and C.
Malaria is more severe and more frequent in people living with HIV.
HIV-positive pregnant women are at particularly high risk of severe malaria.
Insecticide-treated bed nets should be provided to all HIV-positive people in malaria-endemic areas.
Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis also provides some protection against malaria.
Drug interactions between antimalarials and ART must be carefully considered.
Advanced HIV disease is defined as a CD4 count below 200 or the presence of an AIDS-defining illness.

A rapid CD4 count test should be done for all people presenting with advanced HIV disease.
Cryptococcal antigen screening is recommended for all people with CD4 counts below 100.
People with advanced HIV disease are at high risk of death within the first three months of ART.
A differentiated care package for advanced HIV disease includes OI screening, prophylaxis, and ART.
Wasting syndrome is characterised by significant unintentional weight loss in people with HIV.
HIV encephalopathy causes cognitive impairment and neurological symptoms.
Palliative care should be integrated into HIV care for people with advanced disease.
Pain management is an important component of care for people with advanced HIV disease.
Dolutegravir is a preferred first-line ART medicine due to its high efficacy and tolerability.

Nevirapine should not be started in women with CD4 counts above 250.

Abacavir should not be given to people who test positive for the HLA-B*5701 gene variant.
Fixed-dose combination tablets make it easier to take ART by combining multiple medicines in one pill.
Long-acting injectable ART is a new option for people who have difficulty taking daily pills.
